newsitem.title: UK: Iraq offers extra Mar 1-10 Kirkuk cargo - trade.
newsitem.headline: Iraq offers extra Mar 1-10 Kirkuk cargo - trade.

text.p: Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) is offering more Kirkuk crude oil loading in early March on the spot market, Mediterranean refiners and traders said on Friday.
"There is another million-barrel cargo on offer from SOMO for before March 9," said a trader for a Med refiner.

The cargo is extra to six spot contracts totalling 6.05 million barrels approved by the United Nations to bring revenue from the oil-for-food deal close to the $1 billion target for the first three months.

The U.N. approved the spot deals, and an additional term contract with the Indian Oil Corp worth 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) for three months, to compensate for a sharp slide in world prices since the deal was implemented on December 10 last year.
Traders said Kirkuk, loaded at the Turkish port of Ceyhan, has been trading on the Mediterranean spot market at below its Official Selling Price (OSP) of Dated Brent -$1.55 a barrel.

Last week, a million-barrel cargo was sold at OSP -15 cents, equivalent to Dated Brent -$1.70 to a trader. There were conflicting reports over the final destination, some pointing to Romania and others to refineries in southern France or Spain.
A very prompt Kirkuk cargo was also heard sold into Portugal this week at a narrower discount to the OSP. Some traders said the cargo was done at around Dated Brent -$1.60 a barrel, fob Ceyhan.
